newsitem.title: UK: London gold turnover up in Jan vs Dec - LBMA.
newsitem.headline: London gold turnover up in Jan vs Dec - LBMA.

text.p: Daily gold clearance turnover in the London market in January averaged 37.2 million ounces compared with 29.8 million in December, according to figures from the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA).

"The turnover figures show that January was an exceptional month. For the gold price, it was the worst January since 1981, caused by forward selling , fund selling, possibly central bank selling," said bullion market analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The London gold fixing price fell from $367.80 per ounce on January 2 to $345.00, the lowest fixing since September 14, 1993, on January 31.

Smith also noted that the historic 20-day option volatility had risen to around 14 percent at the end of January from four percent in December and the volume of gold futures traded on the Comex exchange in New York volume was up 50 percent in January compared with December.
"This is what happens when the price breaks down through a three-year support level," said Smith.
He said the level of turnover suggested a "digestive problem".
"The professional pipeline could be full. Perhaps the gold is not in safe hands yet," he said.
The value of gold cleared in London averaged $13.20 billion daily versus $11.00 billion in December. Transactions averaged 1,336 daily versus 1,172, the LBMA.

Cleared silver turnover averaged 294.4 million ounces versus 248.8 million in December with average daily value of $1.40 billion against $1.20 billion in December - and on 557 transactions versus 483.
